reviews.text: This game runs surprisingly smooth with just how many things are on the screen, I'm personally having a blast.

I tried to record my impressions as they popped up with the context of going into this blind except for having played (and developed) a roguelite before and being someone who is a little prone to sensory overload: On reaching 2nd map on hard mode I regret this purchase. It's EA yes, but difficulty is not an excuse for enemy or hp sponge spam that inflates the game to make you grind meta currency. - No way yet to change the opacity of "friendly" projectiles. We'll see how hard it gets to see stuff later in the runs. (it does get pretty bad for me on wave 5 onwards) + I like having little "breaks" in between the run where you get to pick up stuff, rest your eyes, and start the next few minutes with a new objective (kill totems or stuff) + I very much love that upgrades aren't just pure stat increases. - Sometimes I struggle to see why I took damage, because I mistake a living enemy for one of the already-defeated corpses that linger just a touch too long. (Or maybe they could turn to be gray when dead.) + I like the ruins(walls) as environmental "strategy" in that I can funnel enemies more or less depending on my build and needs. + Rerolls can drop from vases and enemies. While some will probably consider this "too easy", I do consider it respectful to give me a little more control over RNG in these type of games. - Currently no statistics to check which weapon does how much damage during the run (it shows after though). + Weapons have multiple evolutions. So I already have 2x piercing weapons, I could go for a piercing fireball, or make it chain like lightning... Hell yeah! ? At some point in time I discovered my dash has got a lingering flame carpet effect. I love considering it an additional spell, and I think it could be awesome if we get the chance to alter/upgrade the dash. + Unrelated to the review, but maybe there could be a dash that lets us hop over walls or pass through them (edit: lightning mage got this!) at some point? In general more interaction with the environment (like setting traps, or raising your own wall) could make this stand apart from other survivor-likes. + Visual feedback upon being hit is great. + Price is very fair imo. - Lightning feels super weak compared to fire (but I suppose that'll be balanced later). After my first play session i finished 1 of 2 fire runs and 0 of 4 lightning runs. Oh well. + Level-ups show you which skills they affect (AoE for example). + Meta upgrades (relic system) looks good. You can't just buy everything to use at the same time so you need to make choices, but you still get stronger to some degree. - My first run suddenly ended to my weapons not shooting anymore. I suppose I leftclicked accidentally after a levelup and disabled autoaim, or this was a bug. Sad. I will update the review as I do 2-3 more runs. - Not sure how anyone is supposed to manually cycle through 5 skills to cast them if they are around 1s cd each, so i wish I could force my game to just remain in this auto-cast mode indefinitely. some (of my advise) to get you started: - lightning is weak on its own (unless you evolve storm orb of spark) - especially thunder hammer & chain lightning are worthless, always end up to be only 1-3% of my global dmg dealt - mines sound lame but are actually godsent - the dot that spreads on kill is always op - get something that attacks in a wide (cone) shape or be doomed in stages 5+10 - levels slow down an awful ton after 30 so meta progression becomes a punishing grind - finishing 1 normal run in ruins gives more exp than failing the desert hard stage 4-6 5x - always pick projectile count - combining different status effects is worth more than going for +fire dmg on multiple spells
Every single pixel on my screen is a mob and somehow it doesn't lag a single bit.

Comparing to their previous Soulstone Survivor - which is seems to be built with the same components, several QoL-features are missing, i.e: Spell transparency, healthbars, hide damage numbers etc. The biggest issue (for me) right now that leaves it as a negative review is the lack of description for anything. There's no information other than "Gain the Hypothermia Achievement" to get one of the characters, no explaination as for what any of the "dash" abilities do or what damage they deal. Overall a lack of content but understandable with Early Access. Fun to play but would wait for 1-2 major updates which hopefully adds more spells and/or fixes missing QoL-features.

One night I ate a bunch of chips and salsa with my wife. The really spicy kind, not that tomato sauce you get at the store. Long story short I spent the next day in the bathroom with my steam deck. My wife kept asking me if I was okay but I kept pretending I was sick so I could play this game. She asked me for a divorce. But at least I still have Trials Survivors.

[h2][b]Played on Steam Deck[/b][/h2] This game is going to be great, but can't recommend right now. There is already great variety in the spells. The music is decent enough and the art style is satisfying. For me, this game is way too slow. It takes a long time to get going every stage. The first 30 seconds are usually spent just waiting and the runs take much too long for what is currently in the game. The mobs spawn outside of the arena, and at the start, it can take a good amount of time to get to one without any move speed. You do this 10 times every run. The stages get longer and longer too as you beat runs. I feel if the game was sped up with less rounds and maybe faster rounds I would want to continue playing.

Trials Survivors is a roguelite action title developed and published by Angry Wisp that embraces the increasingly popular survivor-style formula while adding its own emphasis on progression, experimentation, and large-scale combat. Rather than focusing solely on surviving waves of enemies, the game builds its identity around a series of mystical trials where players gradually transform from vulnerable adventurers into devastating forces of destruction. The result is a game that successfully captures the addictive nature of the genre while providing enough customization and long-term growth to keep players invested over multiple runs. The game's central loop revolves around entering combat arenas, completing various objectives, and steadily expanding a character's power through skills, upgrades, and relics. What immediately stands out is the way the game encourages active participation. While some abilities function automatically, others require direct player input, creating a balance between strategic build planning and moment-to-moment action. This approach helps maintain engagement throughout a run, ensuring that players are not simply watching numbers increase while enemies disappear automatically. Positioning, timing, and ability usage remain important even as characters become increasingly powerful. A major strength of Trials Survivors lies in its trial-based progression structure. Instead of relying entirely on endless enemy waves, the game introduces different challenges that require players to adapt their strategies. Objectives vary enough to keep gameplay fresh, encouraging experimentation with different builds and character classes. This variety prevents runs from feeling repetitive and gives each session a sense of purpose beyond simple survival. Every completed objective contributes to character growth, creating a satisfying cycle of risk, reward, and continuous improvement. Build customization is where the game truly shines. Players gain access to a wide range of abilities and upgrades that can be combined in countless ways. The extensive evolution system allows skills to develop into significantly stronger forms, often creating dramatic changes in how a character performs. Discovering powerful synergies between abilities becomes one of the most enjoyable aspects of the experience. Some builds focus on overwhelming projectile spam, while others emphasize area damage, chain reactions, or rapid attacks. This flexibility gives players the freedom to experiment and find playstyles that suit their preferences. Permanent progression also plays a significant role in the overall design. Through relics and long-term upgrades, players can unlock powerful enhancements that carry over between runs. These improvements strengthen future attempts while also opening new possibilities for character development. Features such as increased projectile effects, enhanced damage potential, and additional combat modifiers create a strong sense of advancement. The absence of restrictive level caps further supports the game's philosophy of allowing players to continuously push their characters toward increasingly absurd levels of power. Visually, Trials Survivors prioritizes readability and spectacle. Battles quickly evolve into chaotic displays filled with enemies, magical effects, explosions, and projectiles. The developers clearly designed the game to support large-scale encounters, and the technology behind it handles impressive numbers of enemies on screen simultaneously. Watching an optimized build tear through massive hordes of monsters delivers the kind of satisfying power fantasy that fans of the genre seek. While the visual overload occasionally becomes difficult to track during the most intense moments, it also contributes to the excitement and sense of scale. The game's thematic focus on constellations and celestial trials helps distinguish it from many fantasy-themed competitors. Character progression, world-building, and visual design all connect to this cosmic framework, giving the game a more distinctive identity. Combined with an energetic soundtrack that complements the fast-paced action, the presentation succeeds in creating an atmosphere that feels both mystical and action-packed. As an Early Access release, Trials Survivors is not entirely free from shortcomings. Content variety, while respectable, may eventually feel limited for players who spend dozens of hours exploring every available class and upgrade path. Certain builds can appear significantly stronger than others, leading to balance concerns that will likely require continued refinement. Additionally, the sheer amount of visual effects can occasionally create moments of clutter during high-level encounters. However, these issues are relatively minor compared to the strengths of the core gameplay systems and are common challenges for games still undergoing active development. What ultimately makes Trials Survivors compelling is its understanding of what makes survivor-style roguelites enjoyable. It rewards experimentation, provides meaningful progression, and consistently delivers the thrill of becoming overwhelmingly powerful. The combination of challenging objectives, extensive build variety, and satisfying long-term advancement creates an experience that remains engaging long after the first few runs. Even in its current state, the game demonstrates a strong foundation and considerable potential for future growth. Rating: 8/10

[h1] 《Trials Survivors》简评[/h1] [h3] 爆爽割草！满屏怪物随心割~ [/h3] 《Trials Survivors》是一款画风相当简单而可爱的肉鸽like类幸存者游戏。我们将在游戏中鏖战无尽的怪潮，挺过不同任务的挑战，获得各种星座的力量获得技能并不断升级，在不断强化的怪潮，难度陡增的任务之中生存下去，并达成不错的关卡任务，获得最高级的宝箱，获取大量经验来升级，获得技能，帮助自己更好的杀敌以及生存。 [h3] 核心玩法及亮点 [/h3] 其实，第一眼游戏看起啦还是有点普通的，但是实际上手体验的话，玩起来还是比较上头的，挺爽的割草游戏。而且特效这一块给的还是相当足的，各种特效引导很不错，倒是有咒语旅团的感觉了。而且不管你的职业是什么，也不影响你获取其他属性的星座技能，所以即使你初始是个火法或者雷法，你依然可以获得其他属性的技能。不过当然这一点有好有坏了。 在战斗之中，我们可能会遇到不同的关卡任务，比如护送、歼灭以及生存。护送就是尽量保持在亮光范围内，如果不在范围内，我们的数值条会逐渐减少。这个数值条就代表我们通过此关的评价，评价越高，获得的宝箱越高级。歼灭就是消灭一定量的精英敌人，生存就是活过这一段时间，这个关卡的怪的数量一般来说是最多的。个人感觉其实护送是最难的，因为如果你要保任务指标的话，就必须一直在圈内，而圈是会移动的，你无法很好的躲避怪群。 局内局外的话，成长性也算是双箭头的。我们完成一定的成就或者指标，可以解锁不同的职业，然后通过对战积累经验值的话，会增加我们的圣物槽点数，这可以放置一些我们获得的一些加成，其中有机制向的也有纯数值的，当然也可以通过购买来获得，越高级的占用的越多，所以基本上成长是相互的，我们需要通过战斗来拓宽树脂槽。 [h3] 短板以及不足之处 [/h3] 游戏其实是不错的，不过局内过于随机的技能获取很难受，而且刷新数量很少，虽然能通过杀怪概率掉落，但是概率也低。 技能槽太少了吧。。。容错有点低，很难糊。 [h3] 总结 [/h3] 总的来说，这确实是一款相当不错的肉鸽like类幸存者游戏。整体上游戏还是比较爽的，正反馈也有，但是目前来说的话，存在一定的不足。比如数值方面存在一定问题，而且很难糊，技能槽略少，但是游戏确实是好玩的，值得推荐。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

幸存者游戏的数量泛滥的今天，很多幸存者把东西做的花里胡哨，玩起来都伤眼睛，而本作没有华丽的背景和怪物扰乱视觉，单纯的攻击效果非常丝滑，哪怕上百投射物的技能释放，也能清晰看到特效的落脚点。 游戏的技能看起来不多，但想要体验所有的技能效果怕不是要30+小时往上，因为和传统的固定超武组合不同，技能在满级后会进行进化，进化后又有重新升级的空间，正常不脸黑游玩一局应该是能破百级的。由于没有说明，我对进化机制有点摸不着头脑，技能固定有三个进化分支，进化后不知道和前身有没有关系，因为发射方式和输出逻辑已经发生了很大的变化，就拿最基础的飞刃来说，散射变成永久有个轮子自己追踪，投射物增加就不产生效果了，伤害的很难通过简单判断计算，到底加速度还是加伤害更好，参数有点不明所以。另一个还是投射物的问题，1+1等于伤害翻倍，但是为什么20发的技能投射物也是只+1，起码按百分比加吧，而且在局外成长中，投射物占的容量还挺大的。除此以外，技能好像有隐藏的变形进化，会和其他属性进行混合变形，那么我选的属性加伤就显得很呆。 局外成长方面趋向所见即所得的，和加点不一样，角色会有一个词条容量，想要带什么词条自己装就行，词条来源可以打本爆也可以在商店刷新购买。个人觉得技能的稀有度比较关键，建议优先幸运，但要注意进化后的稀有度是单独的，升级时候的稀有增加就不要选了，看上去数值加的多，除非前期特别困难需要过渡，还是优先升满进化，最为神奇的事情在于，进化完之后，玩家还可以获得同样的基础技能，可以多尝试对比哪个进化更加好用。 流程上采用时间固定关卡，3分钟的时间需要完成目标来积攒宝箱，刷怪生存呆在原地不动就行了，到了时间场上怪会全部爆炸而且经验吸附，就不用那么费精神捡经验。最难的就是护送就需要跟着球东奔西跑，压力很大，虽然更新说降低了概率，但我依旧出现了连续三关都是护送的情况。 感觉就是作者的的创新能力有，毕竟技能进化挺多，而且也比较听劝，更新方向也比较合理及时，但是对数值不太敏感。在没有攻略的情况下，不知道要花多少时间才能把不同的进化摸出来，技能的出现真的很看脸。难度上也是急剧攀升，不知道是策略选错了垃圾技能，还是纯粹的数值不够，感觉沙漠比初始图难打好多。 [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]

Edit 1 (Full Review/15-07-2026): Me : "Wish there is game similar to Vampire Survivor or Soulstone Survivors with fully customizable meta progression". Angry Wisp : "I Gotchu Fam". And then we have this game. The mouse and keyboard control are customizeable, the settings are quite complete with extended (and I mean Extended) language options, the weapons are many with many uniques evolution of their own, the enemies are abundant, and the meta progression is chef kiss. The meta progression using weight system that could be upgraded with profile levels and completeing achievements, while the details upgrades for each character are freely chosen by the player. Developer of the game continuously patch and fix the early access, making the game more comfortable to play with each passing weeks. The latest patch buff-nerf weapons/skills properly as well as adding glossary for weapons evolutions help to create character build to your liking. Waiting for more characters and maps eagerly of this Early Access game. My lovely tiny terminators of in-game character, cute and deadly.

I very much enjoy this game. For under £10 its already only 50p an hour of entertainment and I won't be stopping anytime soon. Devs are currently updating frequently with additions and balances. some abilities and characters are 100% harder to use than others but the devs seem keen to work on that. Different abilities are all quite fun to use and evolve. They feel satisfying and are quite pretty to look at. Currently a varied, even if small range of abilities to use, but again the devs are actively adding new abilities. Gameplay loop feels good. Repetitive in a nice way (easy to chill out with). Progression between runs feels good and unlocking characters is well paced imo. Moving up the difficulties feels nice and the new endless mode is great, so many times my build has only really become powerful in the last missions of the run and the run completes before having a chance to really use it so this is perfect. I've seen some critiques of the escort mission type, idk I like it personally, means you need a build that can hold its own over just finding a chokepoint and hunkering down. Good value game if this kinda thing is your bag. However: At later rounds there's a lot of visual clutter on screen (different mob types, ability spams etc) and multiple times a run I'll lose the mouse cursor so some accessibility or other options to fix that would be great (transparency settings for abilities?, customisable cursor?) I'm also convinced though that if, for example, I design a build for a fire run, every ability APART FROM THE FIRE ONES will cycle through >:0 I'd really like to see some kind of damage merging in future. Fire currently causes ignite and cold causes chill, I think it'd be cool if I hit an enemy with both and it causes another effect like shatter which might ramp up damage the more its hit or something. Just hope the devs stick around :)
